orig.credit: Sun Yat-sen, address at the Whampoa Military Academy (1924)

stanzas: The Three Principles of the People are what our party holds as its foundation;
with them to found the Republic, with them to advance to the Great Unity.
O you many officers, be the vanguard of the people;
early and late, never slackening, follow the Principles.
Vow to be diligent, vow to be brave, be sure to be true, be sure to be loyal;
of one heart and one virtue, carry it through from beginning to end.
Sānmín zhǔyì, wú dǎng suǒ zōng;
yǐ jiàn Mínguó, yǐ jìn dàtóng.
Zī ěr duō shì, wéi mín qiánfēng;
sù yè fěi xiè, zhǔyì shì cóng.
Shǐ qín shǐ yǒng, bì xìn bì zhōng;
yī xīn yī dé, guànchè shǐzhōng.
rom.credit: Romanization: The Epoch Institute (pinyin with tones)

notes: Romanization: Hanyu Pinyin with the citation tones of each syllable (tone sandhi, e.g. of 一 and of two third tones, is not written). 為 in line 3 is read wéi, 'to be, act as'; read wèi it would mean 'for the people, (be) the vanguard'. 'Mínguó' is capitalised as the name of the Republic (民國).
line 1: 吾黨 'our party' is the Kuomintang, whose song this was before it became the anthem; 所宗 'what (we) take as the ancestral, guiding teaching'.
line 2: 大同 (dàtóng), the "Great Unity" or "Great Harmony", the ideal age of the Confucian classics.
line 3: 咨爾 "O you" is an old formula of address; 多士 "the many officers" or "gentlemen".
line 4: 夙夜匪懈 'morning and night without slackening'. 主義是從, 'the Principles (are what we) follow', inverts object and verb with 是 in the classical manner.
line 5: 矢 here is 'to vow, swear' (its classical sense beside 'arrow'). 信 'true, trustworthy, keeping faith'.
line 6: 一心一德 'one heart, one virtue'. 貫徹始終 'carry through from start to finish'; 'it' (the cause) is supplied.
